episode_title: The #1 Mistake Law Firms Make With Their Leads

real_qa.q: What is the number one challenge law firms face when working with marketing agencies?
real_qa.r: The number one challenge is how lawyers operate based on referrals. Even when an agency does great work, lawyers take a very calculated approach to referring partners, often waiting six months to a year to see more results before making referrals, unlike HVAC business owners who immediately justify and promote their purchase to friends.
real_qa.requete: why do law firms delay referrals to marketing agencies

real_qa.q: Why are law firms missing opportunities with leads they generate through marketing?
real_qa.r: The biggest problem is not marketing on the web, but handling the leads that come in. Lawyers often fail to respond to contact forms, answer phones rudely, or don't call people back. Even if a lead isn't a perfect fit, they should still be taken care of; otherwise they will leave negative reviews, damaging the firm's reputation.
real_qa.requete: law firms not responding to leads contact forms

real_qa.q: How does AI search differ from traditional Google keyword ranking for law firms?
real_qa.r: AI search tools like ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini each use different signals to recommend law firms, making it more complicated than the old vanity keyword approach. The old game of pay-per-click and getting page one for vanity keywords is pretty much over, and AI recommends typically three or four firms based on consistency and clarity of messaging.
real_qa.requete: AI search algorithm law firms ChatGPT Claude Gemini signals

real_qa.q: What is Kevin Daisy's background before specializing in law firm marketing?
real_qa.r: Kevin started as a website builder in high school and graduated in 2000. He worked for an engineering firm, then quit after six months to start his first agency in 2006 with no savings or plan. He initially worked with various businesses including hospitals, home services, and doctors before joining Entrepreneurs' Organization (EO) and learning about niching, which led him to specialize in the legal space.
real_qa.requete: Kevin Daisy Array founder background career history

real_qa.q: Why should small law firms focus on their personal brand and local reputation instead of competing on broad keywords?
real_qa.r: Attorneys now need to lean into what's unique, with personal brands more important than ever. People still prefer to work with local attorneys, and big firms like Morgan & Morgan can market heavily but cannot build the local presence that a community-based lawyer can. Small firms should market their uniqueness and local reputation rather than trying to rank for vanity keywords.
real_qa.requete: local attorney reputation versus national law firms marketing
